body: The Dominican Republic has a unique Google car with two metal bars that have thick black stripes on them, and a visible white hood. This car was used for all coverage in the country.
Most utility poles are square and concrete, often with a reverse "L" shape at the top. The Dominican Republic is one of only three places in the Americas with square poles.
Dominican Republic licence plates are pale yellow on top and white on the bottom. The DR is one of the few Latin American countries that does not require front plates.
Roads in the Dominican Republic are often made of smooth, dark-colored asphalt.
Stop signs say "PARE", which is common in South America. Many signs are also attached to yellow signposts.
Street View coverage is very limited, only available in the capital Santo Domingo and the northern city of Santiago de los Caballeros.
Seeing mountains to the north is a definitive clue for being in Santiago de los Caballeros.
Yellow traffic light poles are a good indicator for the city of Santiago de los Caballeros.
Santo Domingo, the capital, has a more developed downtown with tall buildings and wide avenues.
Street name signs in Santo Domingo often have the letters "ADN", for the Distrito Nacional.
Black-and-purple markings on poles are unique to the Santo Domingo area.
The outskirts of Santo Domingo feature a landscape with narrow dirt tracks, whitish dirt, and dried green shrubbery.
Some coverage in Santo Domingo was taken late in the evening, which is not seen in Santiago de los Caballeros.
